title: What if the Moon suddenly disappeared?

lines.text: What if the Moon...
suddenly disappeared?
No explosion. No sound. It's just... gone.
The first thing you'd notice is the dark.
A full moon is about a hundred times brighter than a moonless sky.
From now on, every night is as dark as a new moon.
But the biggest change...
is in the ocean.
The Moon's gravity drives Earth's tides. Without it, only the Sun's pull remains.
Tides would shrink to less than half their size.
Shores that flood twice a day are home to crabs, mussels and sea stars. Their world would shrink to a thin strip.
On coral reefs, the Moon is a clock. Many corals time their spawning by its light.
Without it, they could lose their timing.
Baby sea turtles head for the brightest horizon to find the sea. Without moonlight on the water, more could crawl toward city lights instead.
And that isn't even the strangest part.
The Moon steadies Earth's tilt. The twenty-three and a half degrees that give us our seasons.
Without it, the tilt would wobble more. How much, scientists still debate. But small changes in tilt already help trigger ice ages.
Some scientists even think the Moon's tides helped the first fish crawl onto land.
So the Moon is gone. And Earth keeps spinning...
but it would never be the same planet again.
